samples.summary: locate-surface.test.ts is vacuous: all three assertions hold for a stub that always returns undefined
samples.evidence: The whole suite asserts `toBeUndefined()` three times — no surface (line 13), a sheet surface (line 24), and a doc surface (line 37). In jsdom both locators decline, so every assertion passes for `locateOnSurface = () => undefined`, and would also pass if the dispatch were inverted (sheet routed to the doc locator and vice versa). The test comments explicitly claim "the dispatch reaching it at all is what this asserts" and "which is itself what proves the call reached the doc locator rather than the sheet one" — neither is actually asserted; nothing distinguishes the two branches. The only new production behaviour of this file (which engine answers) is therefore untested. A spy/stub locator per kind, or asserting a formatted address, would be needed.

samples.summary: Migrating locate.ts into the package silently dropped four regression tests that the deleted frontend suite had
samples.evidence: The deleted `packages/frontend/src/debug/locate.test.ts` contained `locatePoint · plausibility` ("describes a region rather than naming a page-sized element" — the 1280×800 `main[data-testid]` case — and "still names a normal control") and `locatePoint · a DOM control over a canvas` ("names the control, not the cell underneath it" and "still asks the engine when the hit-test lands on the canvas itself"). `locate.ts` moved essentially unchanged (only `surface` → `locateOnCanvas`), so all four behaviours still exist in the code, but the new `packages/debug-report/src/ui/locate.test.ts` (96 lines, read in full) has none of them. samples.summary: createDevHost / postJson has no test file at all despite non-trivial new logic
samples.evidence: Glob of `packages/debug-report/src/**` shows no `ui/host.test.ts`. Untested new behaviour includes: the abort timeout (`DRAFT_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the specifically-argued decision to keep the timer armed through `response.json()` (the comment says clearing it early was a bug); distinguishing "no answer within Nms" from "not JSON"; the `error: detail` composition from a non-ok response; `send()` returning a failure when `ref` is not a string; `send()` returning a failure when the server reports `refused` captures; and `currentTheme()`'s three-way fallback. samples.summary: "writes nothing" assertion is vacuous: the temp dir is never given to prepareCaptures
samples.evidence: Line 70 creates `const out = dir()` and line 79 asserts `readdirSync(out)).toEqual([])`, but `prepareCaptures` takes only the capture array — `out` is never passed to it, so a freshly-made mkdtemp directory is trivially empty. The assertion holds regardless of whether decoding writes anywhere, so it provides no evidence for the "decoding and writing are separate" property the comment claims it covers.

samples.summary: The schema fixture is a stub mislabelled as "the real schema", and `expect.any(Object)` makes the output_config assertion unable to detect a wrong schema
samples.evidence: Line 5-6: the comment says "The real schema, imported the way a test may (vitest resolves the alias)" but the value is a hand-written `{ type: 'object' }`; `DRAFT_SCHEMA` is never imported. Line 88-90 then asserts `output_config` equals `{ format: { type: 'json_schema', schema: expect.any(Object) } }`, which passes for any object — so nothing verifies that the schema the caller supplies is the schema sent, and nothing anywhere ties the drafting call to `DRAFT_SCHEMA` (the plugin's `loadCore` path that supplies it is also untested). Asserting `schema` is the identical object passed in `options.schema` would close this.

samples.summary: The `not-configured` outcome — the one the panel's whole degraded path keys on — is never tested

samples.summary: Panel never asserts that an EDITED draft title/body is what actually travels in the bundle
samples.evidence: 'renders the agent’s issue text ... and lets them edit it' asserts only the input's own value; 'sends what was confirmed and reports where it went' uses a host whose `draft` returns no drafts, so the `drafts` map passed to `handOver` is empty. finding.summary: locate-surface.test.ts is vacuous: all three assertions hold for a stub that always returns undefined
finding.evidence: The whole suite asserts `toBeUndefined()` three times — no surface (line 13), a sheet surface (line 24), and a doc surface (line 37). In jsdom both locators decline, so every assertion passes for `locateOnSurface = () => undefined`, and would also pass if the dispatch were inverted (sheet routed to the doc locator and vice versa). The test comments explicitly claim "the dispatch reaching it at all is what this asserts" and "which is itself what proves the call reached the doc locator rather than the sheet one" — neither is actually asserted; nothing distinguishes the two branches. The only new production behaviour of this file (which engine answers) is therefore untested. A spy/stub locator per kind, or asserting a formatted address, would be needed.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The suite's only assertions are three `toBeUndefined()` calls (locate-surface.test.ts:14, 26, 39). In jsdom the sheet locator returns undefined because `gridCanvasBox` finds no canvas under `document.body` (locators/sheet.ts:29-37, 67-68), and the doc locator returns undefined because the zero-sized host rect puts {5,5} outside (locators/doc.ts:53-61) — so the stubbed `cellRefFromPoint`/`cellRect`/`positionAtClientPoint` are never invoked. Every assertion therefore passes for `locateOnSurface = () => undefined`, and also passes with the dispatch inverted: a sheet surface routed to `locateDocPoint` throws a swallowed TypeError inside the try/catch (doc.ts:64-68), and a doc surface routed to `locateSheetPoint` finds no canvas. No global rect/canvas stubbing exists (tests/setup.ts:1-32 only patches ResizeObserver and Blob.arrayBuffer). The in-file comments claim the dispatch branch is proven (lines 24-25, 36-37) but nothing asserts it, and grep shows no other test of `locateOnSurface` — so the one behavior this module owns (which engine answers) is uncovered. Vacuous test presented as coverage for a new behavior: major in this lens.

finding.summary: Migrating locate.ts into the package silently dropped four regression tests that the deleted frontend suite had
finding.evidence: The deleted `packages/frontend/src/debug/locate.test.ts` contained `locatePoint · plausibility` ("describes a region rather than naming a page-sized element" — the 1280×800 `main[data-testid]` case — and "still names a normal control") and `locatePoint · a DOM control over a canvas` ("names the control, not the cell underneath it" and "still asks the engine when the hit-test lands on the canvas itself"). `locate.ts` moved essentially unchanged (only `surface` → `locateOnCanvas`), so all four behaviours still exist in the code, but the new `packages/debug-report/src/ui/locate.test.ts` (96 lines, read in full) has none of them. The two behaviours whose comments in the old file record real past bugs (page-sized promotion, control-over-canvas ordering) are now completely uncovered.

verdict.reason: The new packages/debug-report/src/ui/locate.test.ts has six cases and none exercise the two behaviours the finding names. (1) Control-over-canvas ordering: locate.ts:82-104 declares the hit-test-before-onCanvas order load-bearing and guards with `promoted.tagName !== "CANVAS"` (line 95), yet no test in the repo passes both non-empty `layers` and an `elementAt` returning a meaningful control, and none injects a CANVAS element as the hit — the ordering and the CANVAS guard could be deleted with every test still green. (2) Page-sized promotion through locatePoint: the plausibility gate at locate.ts:103 is never reached by any test with a non-trivial rect (jsdom rects are 0x0, and isPlausibleTarget accepts unmeasured boxes by design per pick.test.ts:263-266). I searched wide: grep for `locatePoint` across the repo shows only locate.test.ts among tests; capture-item.test.ts:33 and overlay.test.tsx:82 both inject a stub `locate`, mocking the unit away; packages/frontend/src/debug/locate-surface.test.ts:5-11 explicitly states the hit-test, promotion and fallback are tested in the debug-report package; no e2e/debug specs exist. The one partial counterexample — pick.test.ts:249-278 unit-testing isPlausibleTarget including the measured 1280x800 rejection — covers the predicate only, not locatePoint's wiring to it, and says nothing about the ordering behaviour. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a behaviour present in the code with no meaningful test covering it (major).

verdict.reason: Verified independently: packages/debug-report/src/ui/host.ts contains substantial runtime logic — postJson's abort-timeout with the deliberately-argued decision to keep the timer armed through response.json() (lines 84-100), the "no answer within Nms" vs. not-JSON distinction (93-101), the error/detail composition for non-ok responses (102-113), currentTheme()'s three-way fallback (35-45), and send()'s two failure paths for a non-string ref (186) and non-empty refused (191).
